China's exports surged 36.3% in September from a year earlier, its customs agency said Wednesday, as pressure ramped up from its trading partners including the European Union to rebalance trade.
The exports data, which was better than what economists had expected, accelerated from the 25% growth in August.
High-tech goods such as semiconductors and autos have helped fuel its rising shipments overseas.
Imports climbed 31% in September year-on-year, also accelerating from August's 28.2% rise.
That resulted in a $133.5 billion trade surplus for China last month, widening from $119.1 billion in August.

The new policy, which goes into effect Wednesday, reduces from 30 to 10 the number of days refugees have to challenge the revocation of their status. The employee was terminated," the statement said.The complaint does not detail what Alfozan might have wanted to do with any captured communications, but the company said the device was sophisticated, designed to evade detection and featured advanced encryption and audio monitoring capabilities.OpenAI said it had evidence the employee planned to place other listening devices throughout other parts of the office building for the purpose of recording meetings."This alleged attempt by a Saudi national to steal sensitive communications from OpenAI was taken extremely seriously. Akasa Air has also suspended flights to Riyadh and Jeddah until the same date.The disruption has spread to international carriers. Emirates cancelled multiple services to Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah and Medina on October 12 and 13, while Etihad Airways cancelled Abu Dhabi-Riyadh flights through October 19 and services to Jeddah and Dammam through October 14. Flydubai has reported cancellations affecting Riyadh, Dammam and Abha through October 19. Qatar Airways has suspended flights to Riyadh and Dammam without announcing a resumption date. Philippine Airlines has extended its Riyadh suspension until November 29.The suspensions come after an attack at Riyadh airport on October 10 killed Indian national Mohammed Yousef Ali and injured 11 others. Four of the injured Indians remain in intensive care, four are receiving treatment in hospital wards and three have been discharged, the embassy said.While operations at Riyadh airport have been suspended, flights at other major Saudi airports, including Dammam, Jeddah and Medina, continue, though they face disruptions. Saudi carriers Saudia and Flynas are operating some scheduled services, according to the embassy.The disruption is forcing passengers to check alternative travel options as airlines adjust their schedules. articles.summary: Indian rupee should be allowed to find its own level, Uday Kotak, Founder & Director, Kotak Mahindra Bank said on Tuesday, asserting that the underlying strength of the Indian economy will reflect in the currency over time.Speaking at theBloomberg New Economy Forum 2026, he said, "My personal view is we should let the rupee find its own level, and over time, the true strength of the economy will play out."The billionaire also emphasised the importance of allowing market forces to determine currency levels without creating expectations about a particular rate that policymakers might seek to defend.Also read: 'If you can't beat them, join them': Uday Kotak backs Chinese investment in IndiaKotak said the situation should serve as an important signal for India to strengthen its competitiveness, improve efficiency and self-reliance, and invest more in research and innovation.A market practitioner, Kotak said, understands what works in financial markets. "Keeping investors uncertain about the level policymakers may be trying to justify can help prevent markets from anticipating official interventions.""My view is a practitioner has the ability of speaking what is going to be effective in markets," he said, adding that policymakers should avoid giving markets a specific level to speculate on.The recent pressure on the rupee was driven more by portfolio investment outflows than by the current account. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) over the weekend announced a slew of measures to stem rupee fall.In a latest move, the central bank announced the creation of a special window for oil marketing companies, which is set to take the dollar demand away from the spot market and tightened rules governing forex derivatives trades to curb speculative bets against the rupee.Following the RBI measures, the Indian rupee strengthened for the third straight session on Tuesday and appreciated 40 paise to close at 95.38 (provisional) against the US dollar.(With inputs from agencies)

articles.summary: New Delhi: Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday said the INDIA bloc's protest against alleged electoral irregularities had a singular objective of restoring democracy in the country.Addressing the gathering after a high tea meeting at his residence with INDIA bloc leaders, opposition MPs and student organisations, Gandhi accused the government of undermining democratic institutions and said the opposition would jointly fight to restore democratic rule."There is no parallel protest; there is one singular protest, and the protest has one mission: the restoration of democracy in India. Democracy has been destroyed, the Election Commission is destroyed, the Constitution is torn up and thrown away. We are fighting together to restore democratic rule in this country," Gandhi said.He also said the opposition would challenge the government's decision to restrict the use of Jantar Mantar as a protest site for expressing democratic dissent.He said, "One method of democracy was Jantar Mantar, but now the government has decided that Jantar Mantar can no longer be used to express democratic feeling, and we are going to challenge that idea. It cannot be so simple for the government to decide that the Indian people will not fight for their voice."He alleged PM Narendra Modi as the main "architect", Home Minister Amit Shah as the "implementer" of destroying the Indian Constitution."The people who have done this: Modi, the main architect; Amit Shah, the implementer; and Gyanesh Kumar. They need to understand that the net is closing around them. It is not going to be so simple that you can destroy the Indian Constitution and get away with it," Gandhi said.After the meeting, Kerala Minister Ramesh Chennithala said the INDIA bloc and the Congress would continue their fight against the Election Commission, alleging that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had damaged the electoral process."We will continue with the fight because Gyanesh Kumar has completely ruined the election process. INDIA alliance and the Congress party will fight to the last. One thing is very clear: everybody is united, and we will fight against the misdeeds of the Central Government and especially Gyanesh Kumar," Chennithala said.He also alleged that a file concerning Kumar's alleged misconduct and corruption during his tenure as Public Works Department (PWD) secretary in Kerala around 20 years ago was being examined by the state government."I received an application regarding the misconduct and corrupt activities of Gyanesh Kumar 20 years back when he was a PWD secretary in Kerala. We are going into the details of the file. In the file, it is very clear that he is involved in various corrupt activities," he alleged."Now, the Kerala government has decided to unearth all these things, and in the coming days, after going into the details, we will take a strong view on these corrupt activities of Gyanesh Kumar.
